checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that the 'ringed tail' checkpoint is untestable due to occlusion/framing. All other checkpoints were accurately assessed as present. The head shape, ear position, eye color, body proportions, coat pattern, and leg striping are all clearly visible and conform to the tabby cat class definition. artifact_review: The Router identified two artifacts: texture anomaly at whiskers (severity 1.5) and structural collapse at lower right torso (severity 2.0). I agree with the whisker smudging observation; the transition from white whiskers to the bright background lacks crispness, showing slight bleeding/melting typical of AI generation in high-contrast zones. However, upon re-evaluation against the Self-Reflection Checklist (specifically Harshness Bias), I must recalibrate my assessment of the lower right torso. While the boundary is soft, it occurs in a deep shadow area where photographic depth-of-field and lighting falloff naturally reduce edge definition. Labeling this as 'spatial grounding failure/melting' was an over-penalization driven by expectation bias rather than definitive visual proof of structural collapse. The fur texture does not exhibit the characteristic 'dissolving' or topological errors of true melting; it is more consistent with underexposure and focus fall-off. Therefore, I am reverting the severity of this issue back to the Router's original assessment of 2.0 (muddy/indistinct boundary) rather than escalating it. The subtle muzzle softness noted previously is within acceptable tolerance for a close-up shot with strong directional lighting and does not constitute a distinct artifact warranting score deduction. Final artifact score adjusted upward to reflect reduced penalty.
